newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Wallowing Brussels bourse waiting for Friday.
newsitem.headline: Wallowing Brussels bourse waiting for Friday.

text.p: The Brussels stock market ended a quietly undulating Thursday with light losses, and traders said all eyes would now be on the overnight performance of the Dow Jones index and Friday's U.S. PPI figures.
"Today we had nothing. Recently we have seen the return of European fundamentals influencing the markets, but now maybe it is the turn of the United States again," one trader said.
U.S. March producer price index figures, expected to show a year-on-year rise of 1.8 percent, are due at 1230 GMT on Friday. March consumer price index data are due at 1230 GMT on Tuesday US-ECI.

Traders said there was a general anticipation that the U.S. Federal Reserve would increase interest rates again in May after having raised them 25 basis points in March, but much would depend on the implications of the strength of the U.S. economy as shown by the inflation figures.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere was the day's main gainer, climbing 1.7 percent to 2,745 francs in a thin volume of 16,000 shares.
Traders said it had benefitted from the strong dollar, high zinc prices and the growing hope the company might finally pay a dividend again, on its 1997 results.
Traders also said there was a growing appetite among investors for cyclical stocks.
Cement maker CBR, a volatile, dollar-sensitive share, climbed 1.6 percent to 3,445 francs.

Retailer Delhaize which has recovered in the past three days from heavy selling on Friday and Monday again spent most of the day in positive territory but ended lower after a late sell order came through.
The share ended 1.4 percent down at 1,755 francs with 99,000 shares traded.
Generale Bank ended 125 francs lower at 13,475 in what traders said was a technical correction after recent strength.
The Bel-20 blue chip share index ended 0.15 points or 0.01 percent lower at 2,120.69 with eight gainers and 12 losers. A total of 1.8 billion francs of Belgian shares changed hands.
